title: The cost of a fragmented tool stack
statusObserved: Public Motion archive available on 2026-10-03. Exact creative current delivery, start date and Meta Library ID were not independently verified.

hook.description: A rapidly increasing cost figure above a presenter turns a familiar software-stack problem into a concrete consequence.

scenes.title: Count the consequence
scenes.visual: Presenter at a desk under a large recurring-cost counter; short supporting captions.
scenes.motion: Number increments and caption replacements; presenter framing remains a stable anchor.
scenes.purpose: Establish an economic pain before naming the alternative.

scenes.title: Make fragmentation countable
scenes.visual: Tool names stack above the presenter, followed by login and invoice counts.
scenes.motion: Quick punch-ins, stacked typography and brief paper-like fragments.
scenes.purpose: Translate an abstract fragmented stack into tangible administrative friction.

scenes.title: Escalate, then introduce the brand
scenes.visual: Annual-cost framing gives way to the ClickUp mark and an integration claim.
scenes.motion: Counter changes, presenter cuts and a large brand reveal.
scenes.purpose: Create the before/after turn.

scenes.title: Replace claims with interface cards
scenes.visual: Task status, document table, whiteboard, chat and clip-menu views appear over the host.
scenes.motion: Individual proof cards slide and replace one another in a consistent screen region.
scenes.purpose: Show recognizable evidence for a broad feature proposition.

scenes.title: Continue the product inventory
scenes.visual: Notetaker/transcript, task creation, scheduling grid and AI-answer card.
scenes.motion: Successive UI replacements with tight framing on each example.
scenes.purpose: Sustain proof cadence without relocating the presenter anchor.

scenes.title: Compress the proposition
scenes.visual: Forms and time tracking conclude the UI sequence; short consolidation statements return.
scenes.motion: Brief color wash, hard type substitutions and a closer presenter shot.
scenes.purpose: Reassemble the many examples into a single proposition.

scenes.title: Price comparison
scenes.visual: A paid-plan card and cost comparison occupy the upper composition.
scenes.motion: Large numbers, plan-card entrance and counter changes.
scenes.purpose: Supply the ad's financial rationale; these figures are not independently verified.

scenes.title: Direct call to action
scenes.visual: Presenter, large start-oriented type and website ending.
scenes.motion: Stable closing composition after the rapid proof sequence.
scenes.purpose: Make the next action easy to identify.

mechanism: Quantify one problem, then answer it through a regular sequence of small interface proofs. The method is useful; the advertised savings are not transferable evidence.
howWeApply: Open Linear with one recognizable work blockage rather than a generic product introduction.
Keep the issue/composer/PR as recurring physical objects instead of borrowing the presenter, colors or financial claims.

title: A missing-link workplace exchange
statusObserved: Public Motion archive available on 2026-10-03. Exact creative current delivery, start date and Meta Library ID were not independently verified.

hook.description: A colleague asks for a link; alternating reactions turn a small familiar request into a coordination problem.

scenes.title: A recognizable question
scenes.visual: Office performer asks another colleague for a link; the reverse view is behind a large monitor.
scenes.motion: Immediate angle reversal with simple captions.
scenes.purpose: Invite recognition before explaining the product.

scenes.title: Which link?
scenes.visual: The same performer plays both sides of a confused exchange about the item and its location.
scenes.motion: Back-and-forth cuts between front and reverse angles.
scenes.purpose: Escalate ordinary friction through cause and reaction.

scenes.title: Reaction payoff
scenes.visual: The clarification culminates in a close reaction and facepalm.
scenes.motion: Tighter framing and a pause on the reaction.
scenes.purpose: Pay off the setup before moving into explanation.

scenes.title: Name the fragmented problem
scenes.visual: Presenter gestures through several places where work can be scattered.
scenes.motion: Caption replacement follows the gestural enumeration.
scenes.purpose: Connect the sketch to an understandable software need.

scenes.title: Show the workspace
scenes.visual: Phone-camera view of a ClickUp task table on a monitor.
scenes.motion: Short pan across the actual workspace.
scenes.purpose: Provide concrete product context after the sketch.

scenes.title: Resolve the exchange
scenes.visual: Presenter returns to explain the unified-workspace idea.
scenes.motion: Moderate punch-ins and hand gestures, without decorative graphics.
scenes.purpose: Tie the demonstrated workspace back to the original question.

scenes.title: Ask for the next step
scenes.visual: Direct-to-camera closing appeal.
scenes.motion: Relatively stable framing and successive captions.
scenes.purpose: Close the conversational argument.

scenes.title: Brand end card
scenes.visual: White background, ClickUp logo and workspace-start call to action.
scenes.motion: Logo entrance followed by a readable end hold.
scenes.purpose: Separate the brand action from the comic setup.

mechanism: A tiny recognizable question creates tension before any product explanation. Alternating cause/reaction shots make a simple premise move.
howWeApply: Use an original developer question on the actual issue object: Bug reported. Now what?
Answer through the documented delegation and draft PR, rather than adding unrelated jokes or unverified speed claims.

title: Short contrast, changing calculator
statusObserved: Public Motion archive available on 2026-10-03. Exact creative current delivery, start date and Meta Library ID were not independently verified.

hook.description: Three compact typography statements contrast productive work, fewer tools and lower cost before any long explanation.

scenes.title: Three compact promises
scenes.visual: Small centered black type on an off-white field changes through a productivity/tool-count/cost contrast.
scenes.motion: Words build and replace; horizontal blur punctuates the substitutions.
scenes.purpose: Deliver a legible proposition quickly.

scenes.title: Interactive cost proof
scenes.visual: A white calculator card shows checked AI-tool categories, a team size and financial totals.
scenes.motion: Cursor toggles rows and the totals update in the same card.
scenes.purpose: Turn the opening abstraction into a changing visual demonstration.

scenes.title: Raise the scale
scenes.visual: Team size increases while a red hand-drawn ellipse calls out an annual figure.
scenes.motion: Number progression and a drawn annotation focus attention.
scenes.purpose: Show the ad's proposed consequence of scale; not a verified economic comparison.

scenes.title: Assignment metaphor
scenes.visual: Small illustrated person becomes an arrangement of agents with a short delegation statement.
scenes.motion: Illustrated characters multiply and regroup.
scenes.purpose: Reduce the workflow relationship to a simple human-to-agent metaphor.

scenes.title: Brand reveal
scenes.visual: Notion cube becomes the wordmark.
scenes.motion: Compact mark-to-wordmark transformation.
scenes.purpose: Name the product after the value argument.

scenes.title: Offer close
scenes.visual: Product positioning and a blue trial-offer button on the same quiet field.
scenes.motion: Minimal change and a readable final hold.
scenes.purpose: Make the advertised next action conspicuous.

mechanism: Sparse typography can feel quick when each replacement advances the argument; one changing proof object then carries the middle of the ad.
howWeApply: Change the meaning of the opening issue card, not merely its color.
Make the same object contract into the actual composer; preserve a clear draft result and brand-faithful palette.

title: An agent builds a bug dashboard
statusObserved: Public Motion archive available on 2026-10-03. Exact creative current delivery, start date and Meta Library ID were not independently verified.

hook.description: A creator introduces converting scattered input into organized work, then demonstrates a specific bug-dashboard request.

scenes.title: Input inventory
scenes.visual: Creator in front-facing footage with a Notion mark and caption emphasis lists several kinds of source material.
scenes.motion: Small framing changes and highlighted words.
scenes.purpose: Establish the breadth of the advertised input problem.

scenes.title: Output promise
scenes.visual: Creator continues with examples of organized outputs before product footage appears.
scenes.motion: Caption replacements dominate a mostly fixed composition.
scenes.purpose: Explain the transformation, at the cost of a long preamble.

scenes.title: Concrete request
scenes.visual: Split-screen product view above the creator; a bug-dashboard request is entered with workspace connectors.
scenes.motion: Typing and a tighter product crop.
scenes.purpose: Convert the general promise into a specific task.

scenes.title: Work begins
scenes.visual: An illustrated agent processing state changes into a dashboard title/table and report-compilation views.
scenes.motion: Processing-state replacement and interface cuts.
scenes.purpose: Make the intermediate work visible.

scenes.title: Material result accumulates
scenes.visual: Source/result rows appear and the bug dashboard fills.
scenes.motion: Rows arrive in a previously sparse table.
scenes.purpose: Show a persistent organized result rather than only a confirmation message.

scenes.title: Inspect the result
scenes.visual: Camera closes in on the table; a row is selected and its detail panel opens beside it.
scenes.motion: Zoom, selection and side-panel reveal preserve the same item.
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate that the generated output can be examined.

scenes.title: Broaden the use cases
scenes.visual: Agent-type grid and a gallery of further examples.
scenes.motion: Pullback into the grid, followed by gallery scrolling.
scenes.purpose: Expand the proposition beyond the initial task.

scenes.title: Creator and brand close
scenes.visual: Brief presenter call to action followed by Notion branding.
scenes.motion: Hard cut from presenter to a clean end card.
scenes.purpose: End on product identity.

mechanism: Request → populated table → opened detail is a useful causal proof chain. The long spoken-looking preamble would be a poor fit for an 18-second film.
howWeApply: Get into the request early, then let the persistent draft PR carry the outcome.
Use a meaningful camera move to inspect the result; do not substitute a feature gallery for a completed workflow.

title: A localization request becomes deliverables
statusObserved: Public Motion archive available on 2026-10-03. Exact creative current delivery, start date and Meta Library ID were not independently verified.

hook.description: A quick human shot leads directly into a selected agent and an urgent, concrete localization request.

scenes.title: Enter the task
scenes.visual: Close human face gives way to a laptop agent catalog and the regional-marketing agent.
scenes.motion: Fast push into the chosen agent card.
scenes.purpose: Move from person to product with almost no preamble.

scenes.title: Type and send
scenes.visual: Tight composer view shows a localization request and deadline, followed by send.
scenes.motion: Camera stays near the typed request and send control.
scenes.purpose: Make the initiating cause readable.

scenes.title: Files arrive
scenes.visual: Progress pill becomes file tiles and an attachments-column view.
scenes.motion: Orange tiles gather, then hard cut/zoom into their destination.
scenes.purpose: Show work materializing as identifiable objects.

scenes.title: Choose a creative
scenes.visual: A medal insert punctuates selection; agent activity resolves into three creative options, followed by a typed choice.
scenes.motion: Metaphor cut, card fan and camera return to the input.
scenes.purpose: Make the human decision alter the next step.

scenes.title: Localize and approve
scenes.visual: One umbrella creative expands into multiple language versions, then an approval prompt receives a thumbs-up.
scenes.motion: Repeated asset identity across transformed cards.
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate a specific transformation and review point.

scenes.title: Refine the formats
scenes.visual: Several size/layout versions appear; a request removes an unwanted carousel.
scenes.motion: Format-card arrangement and return to the agent exchange.
scenes.purpose: Show iterative control rather than one opaque generation.

scenes.title: Handoff for approval
scenes.visual: Attachments and a message go to a reviewer; race-start lights punctuate the waiting stage.
scenes.motion: Send action, metaphor insert and transition to status.
scenes.purpose: Separate preparing deliverables from approval.

scenes.title: Approval changes the outcome
scenes.visual: Waiting status becomes a green check; a coordination agent and ready message appear.
scenes.motion: Status replacement, message reveal and brief celebratory particles.
scenes.purpose: Make the approval state change visible.

scenes.title: Brand close
scenes.visual: Dark monday.com composition with typed agent positioning and logo.
scenes.motion: Typed statement settles into the brand end card.
scenes.purpose: Name the system behind the workflow.

mechanism: The moving objects are the work: one request yields assets, a choice changes them, and approval changes their status. Camera moves follow that causal chain.
howWeApply: Make Linear's send control the origin of the reveal into the actual draft PR.
Carry the same PR card through separation and reassembly; do not add decorative swarms or claim instantaneous completion.

title: A spreadsheet becomes an organized board
statusObserved: Public Motion archive available on 2026-10-03. Exact creative current delivery, start date and Meta Library ID were not independently verified.

hook.description: A deliberately affectionate spreadsheet setup reverses through a broken-heart symbol and a product reveal.

scenes.title: Reverse an expectation
scenes.visual: Spreadsheet field with large type and a heart that becomes broken.
scenes.motion: Kinetic type and symbolic reversal over recognizable work data.
scenes.purpose: Create contrast before the product explanation.

scenes.title: Name the alternative
scenes.visual: Brand letters resolve, then the product homepage start control is clicked.
scenes.motion: Logo assembly and a quick interface cut.
scenes.purpose: Move from argument into a usable product.

scenes.title: Import the existing work
scenes.visual: Import menu, spreadsheet-file selection and a dropzone completion check.
scenes.motion: Macro menu crop, file travel and success-state replacement.
scenes.purpose: Show the migration action instead of only asserting ease.

scenes.title: Continuous before/after
scenes.visual: A sheet is replaced by a populated work board with statuses, people and progress.
scenes.motion: Left-to-right wipe preserves the overall data-table footprint.
scenes.purpose: Make organization visibly change while the subject remains continuous.

scenes.title: Build the planning view
scenes.visual: Large wordplay type punctuates the cut; a planning board gains rows, assignments, statuses and charts.
scenes.motion: Type flies past camera, then structured objects accumulate.
scenes.purpose: Expand the demonstrated transformation.

scenes.title: Comic comparison
scenes.visual: Spreadsheet aside, pixelated face and split comparison columns.
scenes.motion: Rapid cuts and labels falling into two areas.
scenes.purpose: Restate the ad's competitive argument through visual contrast.

scenes.title: Show practical working views
scenes.visual: Dashboard, timeline and workload examples lead to a project comment thread.
scenes.motion: Fast view replacements, then a closer post/reply panel.
scenes.purpose: Tie the broad argument back to concrete work.

scenes.title: Connect and automate
scenes.visual: Condition fields populate and integration icons gather around the board.
scenes.motion: Field filling and icon entrances.
scenes.purpose: Add examples of the advertised system around the same core workspace.

scenes.title: Return to people and schedule
scenes.visual: Live-action workers with UI overlays, then a timeline close-up.
scenes.motion: Human/product cuts and a final interface crop.
scenes.purpose: Humanize the demonstrated workflow.

scenes.title: Trial end card
scenes.visual: Brand and trial-oriented call to action.
scenes.motion: Clear final plate after the dense montage.
scenes.purpose: Conclude with an identifiable next action.

mechanism: A continuous data-object wipe can make a before/after transformation immediately legible. The surrounding jokes and comparison claims are optional, not the mechanism itself.
howWeApply: Transform the issue surface into the agent composer rather than fading between unrelated screens.
Keep the same draft card visible through the review transformation; avoid copying competitive or migration claims.
